title: 14th Sitting of Second session of 2026
presiding: Deputy Speaker Ahmed Saleem opened the sitting; Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla took the chair from agenda item 6 onward, including after the recess
summary: Members first questioned the Minister of Fisheries, Agriculture and Ocean Resources, Ahmed Shiyam, about ice plants, fish aggregating devices (FADs), MIFCO fish purchases and the removal of the UK tariff on Maldivian fish. The main debate was on the government's bill to amend the Waste Management Law (24/2022): ten speeches, mostly in favour, with one MDP member raising concerns about plastic bag fees and utility charges. Debate closed when no one else asked to speak, the bill was accepted for consideration 57-0 and sent to a committee of the whole house, and the Majlis then passed the Human Organ Transplant bill 58-0 after the President had returned it for reconsideration.

items.title: Opening prayers and start of the sitting
Announcement of attendance
items.outcome: 26 present, 6 on leave, 2 on official travel at the opening

items.title: Adoption of the minutes of sittings 7 to 9 (second session of 2026)
items.outcome: adopted as no member had proposed amendments

items.title: Chair's announcements: change to Economic Committee membership
items.outcome: Funadhoo member Mohamed Mamdooh named to the committee in place of North Feydhoo member Ismail Nizar (PNC seat)

items.title: Questions to the Minister of Fisheries, Agriculture and Ocean Resources (6.1, from Kendhoo member Mauroof Zakir, with follow-ups from seven other members)
items.outcome: questions asked and answered by the minister

items.title: Unfinished business: 7.1 debate on the Waste Management Law (24/2022) amendment bill, sponsored for the government by Ungoofaaru member Ibrahim Shifaz
items.outcome: debated, ten speeches; debate closed and sent to a vote

items.title: Committee reports: 8.1 Social Committee report on the Human Organ Transplant bill returned by the President
items.outcome: report presented by Central Maafannu member Asma Rasheed; no one spoke in debate

items.title: Votes: 9.1 accepting the Waste Management amendment bill; second vote on passing the Human Organ Transplant bill as decided by the committee
items.outcome: waste bill accepted 57-0 and sent to committee of the whole house; organ transplant bill passed 58-0

items.title: Close of the sitting
items.outcome: next sitting set for Wednesday 15 July 2026 at 09:00

speakers.name: Ahmed Shiyam
positions: As Minister of Fisheries, Agriculture and Ocean Resources, answered each member on ice plants, FADs, MIFCO purchases and the UK tariff change.
Said Rathafandhoo and Fiyoaree projects are in procurement or reclamation stages, with a Fiyoaree factory targeted around late 2028.
Said replacing cut FADs and building new fish processing capacity is under way, with no firm date given for some sites.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked when the Kudarikilu (B. atoll) ice plant promised by the President will start operating.
Asked about a way for reef fishers to sell to resorts and when the Hulhumale' fish factory and MIFCO purchases at the promised price begin.
On the waste bill, supported it overall and urged easy arrangements for councils to work with nearby resorts on island waste.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked about a sports-fishing buoy near Vaikaradhoo that was cut loose, delays in replacing FADs, MIFCO reef fish buying and a sea-side facility.
On the waste bill, said he had mixed up the law number earlier and supported the amendments, noting the wider waste categories and island processing.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Asked what benefit lifting the UK tariff on Maldivian fish would bring to Maldivian fishers.
On the waste bill, fully supported it and thanked the sponsor, saying it settles administrative confusion left unresolved by earlier governments.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Asked how long the Makunudhoo ice plant, out of service for over three years, will stay unrepaired, and how farmers on two islands can get fertiliser.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Asked when the FAD near Dhiffushi, cut on 5 February, will be reinstalled and what is being done so Male' atoll benefits from ocean resources as land reclamation spreads.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked whether more FADs are planned for Baa atoll and requested the details.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Said dollar earnings from fisheries fell between 2018 and 2023 and are now rising, and asked what explains the turnaround.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Asked when the Rathafandhoo ice plant work will start, when the Faresmaathodaa ice plant will be repaired and when the Fiyoaree factory will be finished.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said he backs the aims of the amendments but is concerned that waste from non-industrial islands could be sent to populated islands.
Suggested banning shops from handing out plastic bags instead of the MVR 2 charge, and asked for limits on waste and utility fees.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Said the government wants modern, digitised waste management and criticised the previous administration's record on waste and dollars.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the amendments, saying the bill clarifies the duty on plastic bags, regional waste centres and the roles of the EPA and utility regulator.
Called for committee scrutiny of WAMCO's finances and of the Vandhoo waste project.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Said councils lack money to manage waste and proposed fixed timelines for service, resort help and a ban on burning waste near homes.
Asked that WAMCO lower fees for atoll islands.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Strongly supported the bill, saying councils can partner with resorts and the roles of regulators become clearer, and criticised the opposition's waste record.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the amendment, saying residents want island waste systems and a WAMCO office has been set up in his constituency.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Said the waste company was created to fix past dumping, urged more private sector role, and asked for support for residents near a landfill site in his area.

speakers.name: Asma Rasheed
positions: As Social Committee rapporteur, presented the committee's report on the Human Organ Transplant bill that the President returned for reconsideration.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 7 to 9 of the second session of 2026 adopted.
Economic Committee membership changed: Funadhoo member Mohamed Mamdooh replaces North Feydhoo member Ismail Nizar.
Waste Management Law (24/2022) amendment bill accepted for consideration and sent to a committee of the whole house.
Human Organ Transplant bill passed by the Majlis as decided by the Social Committee, with no amendments proposed on the report.
Next sitting set for Wednesday 15 July 2026 at 09:00.

votes.what: Accept the Waste Management Law (24/2022) amendment bill for consideration
Pass the Human Organ Transplant bill as decided by the Social Committee
